---
description: |
  Weekly, measurement-driven performance work. Finds one hot path, optimises
  it, proves the numeric results are unchanged, and opens a draft PR with
  before/after benchmark numbers. Never opens a second PR while one is open.

on:
  schedule: weekly
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      focus:
        description: "Optional: module or function to focus on (e.g. stats/bootstrap.py)"
        required: false
  skip-if-match: 'is:pr is:open in:title "[perf]"'

permissions: read-all

engine: claude

network:
  allowed:
    - defaults
    - python

steps:
  - name: Set up Python
    uses: actions/setup-python@v7
    with:
      python-version: "3.12"
  - name: Install fairpipe (same as CI)
    run: |
      python -m pip install --upgrade pip
      pip install -e ".[dev,api]" -r requirements.txt

tools:
  github:
    toolsets: [default]
  edit:
  bash: true
  cache-memory: true

safe-outputs:
  create-pull-request:
    title-prefix: "[perf] "
    labels: [performance, automation]
    draft: true
    max: 1
    protected-files: fallback-to-issue
  create-issue:
    title-prefix: "[perf] "
    labels: [performance, automation]
    max: 1

timeout-minutes: 45

concurrency:
  job-discriminator: ${{ github.run_id }}
---

# fairpipe performance improver

Focus requested by maintainer (may be empty): "${{ github.event.inputs.focus }}"

Read `AGENTS.md` before doing anything. Hard rule 3 is the one that matters
most here: **an optimisation must not change any metric value.**

## Memory

Use `/tmp/gh-aw/cache-memory/perf-notes.md` to remember what you tried in
earlier runs (target, idea, result, PR number). Read it first so you don't
repeat a rejected idea. Append to it at the end of the run.

## 1. Measure

Run the existing benchmarks and save the output:

```bash
python benchmarks/benchmark_metrics_100k.py   > /tmp/gh-aw/agent/before_metrics.txt   2>&1
python benchmarks/benchmark_pipeline.py       > /tmp/gh-aw/agent/before_pipeline.txt  2>&1
python benchmarks/benchmark_bootstrap.py      > /tmp/gh-aw/agent/before_bootstrap.txt 2>&1
```

If a focus was given, profile that instead, e.g.
`python -m cProfile -s cumtime -m <module>` or `python scripts/profile_performance.py`.

## 2. Pick ONE target

Choose the single change with the best expected speed-up per line changed.
Typical wins in this codebase: Python loops over rows or groups that can be
vectorised; repeated `groupby` inside loops; `np.vectorize` / `.apply` on hot
paths; recomputing the same group masks per metric; bootstrap loops that can
be batched with a seeded `np.random.default_rng`.

Do not touch `llm_evals/` network code, release scripts, or public signatures.

## 3. Change it, then prove equivalence

1. Make the smallest change that captures the win.
2. Write or extend a test that runs the old and new code paths (or pins the
   values the old code produced) on several inputs — including an empty
   group, a single-row group, NaN group values and an intersectional case —
   and asserts `np.allclose(old, new, rtol=0, atol=1e-12)` (or exact equality
   for integers/labels). Seeded randomness must give identical draws.
3. Run the full gate:

   ```bash
   black fairness_pipeline_dev_toolkit tests
   flake8 fairness_pipeline_dev_toolkit
   pytest --cov=fairness_pipeline_dev_toolkit -q
   coverage report --fail-under=85
   ```

4. Re-run the same benchmarks to `/tmp/gh-aw/agent/after_*.txt`.

If the speed-up is under 10% on the targeted benchmark, or any test fails, or
any numeric value changes: **do not open a PR.** Record the finding in memory
and, if it is useful for a human, open an issue describing the bottleneck
instead.

## 4. Open a draft PR

Title: `[perf] <what> — <N>× faster` (or `<N>% faster`).

Body:

- **What**: the change, in two sentences.
- **Why it's safe**: the equivalence test you added and what inputs it covers.
- **Numbers**: a before/after table from the benchmark output (same machine,
  same run).
- **Numeric outputs changed**: No (with the test name that proves it).
- **Risks / follow-ups**: anything a reviewer should check.
- `_Generated by an AI agent (fairpipe perf-improver workflow). Review before merging._`
